hints.title: Recursive Equivalence Symmetry
hints.text: Two binary trees are flip equivalent if one can be transformed into the other by a sequence of left-right subtree swaps.

hints.title: Base Case Comparison
hints.text: If both nodes are null, they are equivalent. If only one is null or their node values differ, they are not equivalent.

hints.title: Branching Subtree Checks
hints.text: When root values match, test both cases: either subtrees match without flipping (left1 == left2 and right1 == right2), or they match with flipping (left1 == right2 and right1 == left2).

hints.title: See the blueprint

variables: N: number of nodes in smaller tree
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Trying all 2^N possible subtree flip states globally produces exponential runtime.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Since node values are unique, at each node at most one of the two branches can succeed, keeping runtime linear.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should handle null checks cleanly and state clearly why uniqueness of node values bounds execution to O(N).
complexity.notes: If values were not unique, runtime would be bounded by O(4^(depth)).
